channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [8] Manipulation of ferromagnetism with a light-driven nonlinear Edelstein-Zeeman field
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Joseph Checkelsky, Fahad Mahmood

Authors: Yinchuan Lv, W. Joe Meese, Azel Murzabekova, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental control of magnetism in a van der Waals magnetic semiconductor, relevant to quantum materials.

Tags: #experiment #magnetism #vanderWaals

Abstract: Ultrafast non-thermal control of magnetism is a major goal of spintronics, however, in centrosymmetric materials, symmetry typically forbids direct control via electric fields. Here, Lv, Meese and coauthors use the non-linear Edelstein effect to create a non-equilibrium magnetic density in the van der Waals magnetic semiconductor Cr2Ge2Te6.
